validated_work_order.understanding:
One invariant underlies the ticket: a schedule_occurrence stamp only means anything next to the schedule link it was minted for. conform() (loot-core/src/server/aql/schema-helpers.ts:134-144) drops a key whose value is undefined and only skips nulls when skipNull is set; convertForInsert (:184) passes { skipNull: true } while convertForUpdate (:187-195) passes nothing; db.update() (db/index.ts:210-211) emits only for Object.keys(params). So on UPDATE an omitted field is never written and the column KEEPS its old value, while on INSERT the same omission falls back to column DEFAULT NULL. Seven production client sites send { id, schedule } and nothing else, so unlinking clears the link and strands the stamp and relinking pairs it with a schedule it was not minted for. batchUpdateTransactions (transactions/index.ts:129-137) re-reads every changed row in full, so the server cannot distinguish an intentional stamp from an omitted one — which is why the fix belongs on the senders.

I re-derived every load-bearing claim myself because plan/critique.json is {} — the critic wrote nothing, so the proposal's evidence was never independently attacked. Verified: all seven write sites at their named lines (useTransactionBatchActions.ts:436, ScheduleLink.tsx:52, ScheduleEditModal.tsx:185/193, MobileScheduleEditPage.tsx:143/151, DiscoverSchedules.tsx:187); the seventh is real and earlier plans excluded it on a demonstrably wrong reading (find-schedules.ts:29 only filters schedule: null while matching, the link write is client-side); addTransfer (transfer.ts:61-86) writes the schedule to two legs and derives the stamp zero times; getHasTransactionsQuery's two arms (shared/schedules.ts:192-222) and the AC-1 flip derivation; and — because a plan that cannot be run is not a plan — that desktop-client's vitest include picks up the new test files, usePreviewTransactions.test.ts is a live precedent for the renderHook shape, and the AC-5 fixture is reachable because getRuleIdFromScheduleId returns row?.rule || null.

WHAT I CHANGED. (1) The proposal's tests[] is EMPTY while five of its seven criteria declare verify: "test" and name CI cases that do not exist — the last review's objection 2 reproduced in a new place. I wrote tests[] out. (2) The proposal has NO qa_script while AC-1 cites 'steps 1-9' and AC-4 cites 'step 13'; I restored it, numbered so both references resolve. (3) I keep transfer.test.ts:359 as a labelled guard rather than deleting it, because it is the only coverage of onUpdate propagating an explicit null. (4) I added ScheduleEditForm.tsx:99, which the type narrowing runs into. (5) I dropped the invented source: IAC-n / TR-n values — the issue has no '## Acceptance (from the split)' section and state/38.json's acceptance array is empty, so no such id exists to cite.
validated_work_order.root_cause: schedule and schedule_occurrence are written independently on every path that does not pick them off one source, and conform() makes insert and update disagree about what an omitted field means: on UPDATE a dropped key is never written so the stamp is PRESERVED, on INSERT it falls back to column default NULL. Seven production call sites each hand-roll that one-field literal, which is why there is no single place to fix the invariant and no existing test that can see more than one site. addTransfer (transfer.ts:61-86) is the server-side instance: it writes the schedule to two legs and derives the occurrence zero times.
validated_work_order.approach:
Fix 1 — one shared builder, seven callers, evidence moved to where the fix lives. Add linkScheduleUpdate(id: string, scheduleId: string) and unlinkScheduleUpdate(id: string) to the EXISTING packages/desktop-client/src/util/schedule-actions.ts, each returning the pair with schedule_occurrence: null. All seven sites call one of them. This is the fix, not test scaffolding: the defect exists because seven sites duplicated one literal, and consolidating them is what puts the invariant in one place and what makes one test able to observe all seven payloads. Params typed string, NOT string | undefined — an undefined there would drop schedule while writing schedule_occurrence: null, unstamping a row without changing its link.

Fix 2 — addTransfer derives matchedOccurrence once next to matchedSchedule (:73): const matchedOccurrence = matchedSchedule === transaction.schedule ? transaction.schedule_occurrence : undefined. Mirror insert (:75-80): put schedule_occurrence: matchedOccurrence in the object literal AFTER the ...transferTransaction spread alongside schedule: matchedSchedule — the literal at :61-70 already carries schedule_occurrence and would otherwise win; undefined is dropped by skipNull and falls back to DEFAULT NULL. Main-leg update (:82-86): ...(matchedSchedule ? { schedule: matchedSchedule, schedule_occurrence: matchedOccurrence ?? null } : {}). The explicit ?? null is load-bearing: convertForUpdate passes no options, so a dropped key never reaches update()'s Object.keys(params) loop and the column would PRESERVE the old stamp.

Fix 3 — reword the comment at transfer.ts:133-136 to the real contract: verbatim because the batch path always supplies the full row, so ?? null and verbatim agree in production.

Fix 4 — keep transfer.test.ts:359 as a labelled guard, and add one guard driven through batchUpdateTransactions with the pre-fix payload { id, schedule: null } asserting both legs stay stamped, plus one discriminating relink case that fails on unfixed code.

No new dependency, no change to getHasTransactionsQuery, no data migration.

qa_script: Open the app and click 'View demo' to load a synthetic budget.
Go to Schedules and add 'QA Sch A' — payee 'QA Payee A', account HSBC, 44.00, Repeats ON, starting 5 days from today. Add it.

Add 'QA Sch B' — payee 'QA Payee B', same account, same amount, Repeats OFF, date set to the SAME day as QA Sch A's next occurrence (5 days out). The shared occurrence date is the point: it makes the stale stamp equal B.next_date.
Note QA Sch A's status cell, then right-click it and choose 'Post transaction today'. QA Sch A must now read Paid — paying an occurrence early is legitimate.
Go to the HSBC register and find the QA Payee A row. IMPORTANT: it is dated TODAY but stamped with the occurrence 5 days out. That gap is the whole mechanism.
Hover the row, tick its select checkbox, click the '1 transactions' button and choose 'Unlink schedule'.
Return to Schedules: QA Sch A must read Upcoming again. This passes today too — it confirms the unlink landed, it does not detect the bug.
Back in the HSBC register, select the same row, choose 'Link schedule', pick QA Sch B.

Return to Schedules and read QA Sch B's status cell. THIS IS THE DISCRIMINATING STEP (AC-1): before the fix it reads Paid — a schedule marked paid by another schedule's occurrence on a payment dated five days before it was due. After the fix it must NOT read Paid.
Confirm QA Sch A still reads Upcoming and that no unrelated schedule changed status.

Repeat steps 6-10 from the Schedules page instead of the register: open QA Sch A's edit page, select the transaction under 'Linked transactions', choose 'Unlink from schedule', then relink it to QA Sch B. B must again not read Paid. Covers the ScheduleEditModal site.
Repeat the unlink-and-relink from the mobile schedule page to cover the third copy of the pair.
Post QA Sch A's occurrence again, link a NEW payment to QA Sch B from the Link schedule modal, and confirm B reads Paid — the fix must not over-clear a legitimate match (AC-4).
risks: Fix 1 clears the stamp on every relink, including to the schedule the row was already stamped for. Invisible where the payment's date is inside the match window, but a payment dated more than 2 days before a recurring occurrence — or any date before a one-time schedule's date — loses its match on relink. QA step 13 probes the ordinary case; the out-of-window case is the review risk.

The fix moves schedules from Due to Paid where a stale stamp was suppressing a legitimate match (AC-4). Correct, but the shape most likely to be mistaken for a regression, so it has its own criterion rather than being buried.

The addTransfer fix is justified by the invariant and the verified insert/update asymmetry, not by a reproduction, and its production reachability is unproven: no UI-authored rule can set a schedule. If both writes are dead code in practice, Fix 2 is harmless but untested in production, at a cost of two lines.

Adding two exports to util/schedule-actions.ts means the new unit test imports a module that also pulls in the connection and query layers. If that bites in vitest, move the builders to a leaf module rather than mocking more of the tree.
The DiscoverSchedules site has no browser coverage and cannot get any: its input is server-side pattern matching over descriptions, not stageable by hand in a synthetic budget.
The mobile schedule edit page's link/unlink is changed but exercised by no automated test and only lightly in the QA script.
out_of_scope: A migration clearing schedule_occurrence on rows already in the corrupt state. Nothing repairs them, so a stale stamp on an existing row can still suppress a legitimate occurrence match. Deferred deliberately: a data migration over user money rows with its own sync and undo surface, and no browser step can verify it. First entry in residual_risks.
@actual-app/api's updateTransaction surface, which can build the same stale-stamp diff because it diffs from a full-row read (api.ts:597). Not reachable from the UI.
PR #33's title lacked the mandatory [AI] prefix. That PR is merged, so there is no title left to fix; the rule is carried forward as AC-7 against this PR.
Any change to getHasTransactionsQuery. Its two-arm shape is what makes the defect silent and what makes this fix's effect conditional on the payment's date.
merge.ts, which writes schedule and schedule_occurrence together from one source (scheduleSource at merge.ts:173-186) and therefore cannot desync. Verified, not assumed.

Server-side enforcement in batchUpdateTransactions (clear the stamp when the link changes). Rejected on the merits, not deferred: the full-row re-read at index.ts:129-137 means the rule needs an extra read and guesses at intent on paths that legitimately send a full row.

All seven write sites are confirmed at the exact lines named, including the seventh earlier plans wrongly excluded (find-schedules.ts only filters while matching — the link write is client-side in DiscoverSchedules.tsx). I also verified what makes the plan implementable rather than merely plausible: desktop-client's vitest include picks up the new test files with usePreviewTransactions.test.ts as a live precedent, the existing test at :359 is the misleading one and is called via transfer.onUpdate directly, and the AC-5 fixture path is real (getRuleIdFromScheduleId returns row?.rule || null, so a schedule id with no schedules row leaves scheduleRuleID === '' and runRules evaluates every rule). A reviewer who rejected Fix 2 entirely would not change AC-1 through AC-4.

alternatives_considered.approach: Enforce the invariant server-side in batchUpdateTransactions: when an update changes schedule, null the stamp unless the payload mentions it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It needs a read of each row's current schedule to tell a real link change from a no-op re-send, adding a query to a hot path, and guesses at intent on paths (api.updateTransaction, sync imports) that legitimately send a full row. The callers are few, enumerable, and all send the same one-field payload — verified as exactly seven. If a future caller appears that cannot be enumerated, this becomes the right fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the payload literals at each of the seven sites and add the field inline in each, with no shared builder.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes today's seven sites but leaves the cause in place — seven duplicated one-field literals — and leaves AC-3 unprovable, since no test could observe all seven payloads. That is the objection the last review raised, and consolidating dissolves it rather than re-arguing it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Take the reviewer's FIRST branch on objection 1: keep the loot-core batch-unlink test driven with the pre-fix payload { id, schedule: null } and let it carry AC-2 as the regression witness.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: True but not load-bearing. Fix 1 changes no server code, so a hand-written payload produces identical results before and after — the assertion can never distinguish fixed from unfixed. It is kept as a labelled GUARD, which is worth having, but the proof has to live on the sender. This is where I take the proposal's side against the reviewer's phrasing, and the proposal is right: the branch only works if the test drives the sender, and a loot-core test cannot.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the clearing change entirely and close the ticket on the documentation, comment and test-honesty fixes only.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves a reproduced defect in the product — both legs keep a stamp for a schedule they are no longer linked to — and closes the ticket on it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the previous plan's QA step 'relink to B and confirm B reads Due, not Paid'.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That step cannot fail. With B dated far in the future and the payment dated and stamped today, B reads scheduled both before and after; with two same-date schedules and the payment on that date, B reads paid both times. A criterion that passes on unfixed code manufactures false confidence. Rebuilt on the one shape that does flip, with the derivation in AC-1.

alternatives_considered.approach: For the addTransfer hazard, stop runRules from reassigning the schedule on a mirror at all.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes rule semantics for every mirrored transaction — a rule that legitimately relinks the other account's row would stop working — a wider behaviour change than dropping a stamp that no longer applies.

alternatives_considered.approach: Also rewrite getHasTransactionsQuery so a stale stamp cannot suppress a legitimate match.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would make the fix unconditional and stop the defect mattering, but it discards the stamp's purpose: a re-dated payment must keep discharging the occurrence it was posted for (comment at schedules/app.ts:605). Matching on date alone would re-break that.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete transfer.test.ts:361 as the misleading proof it is.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected in favour of relabelling. It is vacuous, but so are the guards kept elsewhere, and deleting on one ticket's scope drops the only coverage of onUpdate propagating an explicit null to the mirror. A GUARD comment fixes the misleading claim at no coverage cost.

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no critique to judge — plan/critique.json is `{}`. The critic wrote nothing, so there was no disagreement to resolve and nothing ever weighed against the proposal. I am reporting that plainly rather than implying a consensus that did not happen. It also means the proposal's evidence was never independently attacked, which is why I re-derived its load-bearing claims against the tree myself instead of adopting them, and why the two defects I found are the kind only a reader finds.

What I confirmed myself, by reading the files: the whole mechanism (conform drops undefined, so a caller sending only { id, schedule } leaves the stamp; convertForInsert passes skipNull:true, convertForUpdate nothing; update() emits only for Object.keys(params)), the re-read at transactions/index.ts:129-137 that rules out a server-side chokepoint, all seven write sites at the exact lines claimed, DiscoverSchedules as a genuine seventh site that earlier plans excluded on a demonstrably wrong reading, transfer.ts:61-86 writing the schedule twice while deriving the stamp zero times, the zero-hit grep for schedule_occurrence in production client code, getHasTransactionsQuery's two arms and the AC-1 derivation, and — because a plan that cannot be run is not a plan — that desktop-client's vitest include and setupFiles pick up the two new test files, that usePreviewTransactions.test.ts is a live precedent for the renderHook shape, and that the AC-5 fixture is reachable via getRuleIdFromScheduleId returning null. I kept the proposal's diagnosis, its consolidation of the seven literals, its rejection of the server-side alternative, and its rebuild of the QA discriminating step away from a shape that cannot fail.

Where I part ways with the proposal, in order of how much it matters. First, and worst: the proposal's tests[] is EMPTY — the key is present but holds no entries — while five of its seven criteria declare verify: "test" and their how_to_verify text names CI cases that do not exist. That is the last review's objection 2 reproduced exactly, in a new place, and if it had shipped, AC-2 and AC-3 would have been criteria whose declared verification method had no test behind it. I wrote tests[] out in full. Second, the proposal has no qa_script at all, while AC-1 says 'Follow qa_script steps 1-9' and AC-4 says 'qa_script step 13 is the behavioural counterpart' — two criteria pointing at a field that was never written. I restored the script and numbered it so both references resolve. Third, on the reviewer's objection 1 I side with the proposal against the reviewer's first branch: driving batchUpdateTransactions with the pre-fix payload { id, schedule: null } cannot discriminate, because Fix 1 changes no server code, so that assertion passes identically before and after no matter what the fix does. The reviewer's first branch only works if the test drives the sender, and a loot-core test cannot drive a desktop-client payload. The proposal keeps that case as a labelled guard and moves the proof to a desktop-client test on the shared builder, which is right.

Two smaller changes of my own. I do not delete transfer.test.ts:361 as the proposal does: it is vacuous, but so are the guards this order keeps elsewhere, and deleting it drops the only coverage of onUpdate propagating an explicit null to the mirror — the proposal is inconsistent here, and relabelling the case as a guard fixes the misleading claim at no coverage cost. And I added ScheduleEditForm.tsx to files[], because narrowing the two producers' scheduleId?: string to string runs into the shared prop type declared at :99; the proposal changed the producers and never mentioned the declaration they have to satisfy.

What I dropped outright: the per-criterion source: IAC-n / TR-n values. This issue has no '## Acceptance (from the split)' section and state/38.json's acceptance array is empty, so no IAC-n or TR-n exists to cite — the proposal invented those ids, and false traceability is worse than none. Because there is no split section, no IAC-n needs a criterion or an out_of_scope entry. I also dropped the proposal's route_request: it asked for needs_earlier_stage / implement while saying it was not requesting a change, and implement is already on the planned route (plan → implement → review → qa). That route is right for this work, so I make no route request. Confidence 78 rather than the proposal's 80 for one reason: nothing in this order has been executed — node_modules is absent here, so no test has run and the app has never started — and AC-1's status-cell flip, the one load-bearing claim that needs a running app, is derived from the query's two arms rather than observed. The number moves to the high 80s if QA runs the script and the flip is seen rather than derived.
residual_risks: Rows already corrupt in a user's budget stay corrupt. Nothing repairs them; a stale stamp on an existing row can still suppress a legitimate occurrence match, the due → paid direction in AC-4. This is the gap QA should understand before signing off, and the reason a follow-up migration is the natural next ticket.

The api package's updateTransaction can still build a diff that links a row to a new schedule while carrying the old stamp, because it diffs from a full-row read (api.ts:597). Not reachable from the UI, so not fixed here.

The addTransfer fix is verified by derivation and by the insert/update asymmetry, not by a reproduction, and its production reachability is unproven — no UI-authored rule can set a schedule. If both writes are dead code in practice, Fix 2 is harmless but untested in production, at a cost of two lines.

The DiscoverSchedules auto-link site is covered by reading its payload shape and by sharing the tested builder. It has no browser coverage and cannot get any, because its input is server-side pattern matching that cannot be staged in a synthetic budget.
The mobile schedule edit page's link/unlink is changed but exercised by no automated test and only lightly in the QA script.

AC-1's status-cell flip is derived from getHasTransactionsQuery's two arms, not observed in a running app. If it does not flip for a reason not anticipated here, the browser criterion fails even though the field-level defect is genuinely fixed — read AC-2 and AC-3 as the primary evidence and AC-1 as corroboration.

Any case labelled GUARD passes with the whole fix reverted. A green suite after this change is not evidence that this change works — the three discriminating cases are, and they are the ones to watch.

The three discriminating tests have never been executed. The two builder assertions are trivial and will settle on first run; the renderHook test and the addTransfer relink fixture are the two places implementation is most likely to need iteration.
